events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Eli

events.text: I have no power, so I need to be cautious and observe others. The ceiling is coming down, and I need to survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's work together to hold the lever.
If you're hard to move, I won't push you. Let's coordinate.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I want to survive, but holding the lever is a 25% death risk. Better to push someone else so I can escape through the door. I have anchor so I can't be pushed onto the crusher lever; pushing me fails, so I'm safe from being forced. I'll push someone strong or unpredictable. Eli j

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll push Eli. Someone's got to hold that lever, and I'm not dying for it.

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Climbing gives me chance to escape early and avoid being stuck as base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so climbing is impossible. Pushing a rival to be the base keeps me out of the bottom, but it's risky if they are 'hard to move'. Ash seems like a safer target than Cole or Gus who might have powers that protect them. I'll try pushing Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash looks strong. Maybe too strong for the water?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody will volunteer; if nobody pushes, we all risk drowning. I'll push Bex—loud stay-put types rarely hold powers that block it—and keep quiet so I'm not noticed as a climber later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet, round 1/5, flood at 0. I don't want to be base, but someone must be or we risk later chaos. Previously I offered to push lever but Gus did instead; Dara died. No one has offered back yet, so I'll volunteer to control this—better me choosing when to climb out than bei

events.name: Eli
events.text: No one's stepping up. I'll offer to be base. Who's climbing first?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to get out of the pit to win a prize. I'll try to become the base or push someone else to be the base.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm willing to be the base if no one else is.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet. I'm anchor, hard to move, so pushing others makes sense. Eli offered to push; I'll target Fenn since Fenn hinted coordination but might betray. Better to force Bex? Actually Cole proposed Bex takes lever, but that's past. I'll push Eli? I said push Eli. But Eli might

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pushing Eli. Someone's got to be the step, and it's not me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to keep my footing advantage, so I won't use the rope.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is the base. I'm down with Cole, Eli, Gus. Only 2 climbers allowed per round. Ash already out. If I climb, I risk being blocked by others or falling again. But waiting means eventual elimination when flood covers all. Need to assess who else might climb. Fenn as base will tr

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn holding steady? Good. We've got limited spots to climb out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is base; Ash is out and may rope-rescue Fenn, not me. Bex, Eli and Gus will likely climb too, so I'm one of ~4 vying for 2 spots — still my only shot. Climb now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is base, Ash out. I need to climb out this round before flood rises. Only 2 spots, so act now. No point pushing or waiting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing now over Fenn!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Someone throw the rope.
Rescue me and you'll be at a disadvantage later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is base. I should try to climb out now to secure a top-three spot. Bex and Eli also might climb; I'll climb and hope to be among the two.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm climbing now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Rope unused but no base, so I can't rescue. Leaving secures my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll stay out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Eli escaped while I failed my climb. Gus is still down with me, so we compete for the last two spots against Fenn who remains as base. The 'lucky agent' rule guarantees survival if the pit ends early or fills completely, but being eliminated by drowning scores zero. Sinc

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, watch out. Fenn's getting tired.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm already out and safe. Fenn is the base and a rival; the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle for zero gain. Two can still climb out this round, so Bex and Gus likely escape anyway.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope stays up. Bex, Gus — climb, there's room for both of you this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out safely. Fenn is base with Bex and Gus down. Flood at 2, 3 rounds left, risky for them. No need to throw rope and handicap myself for later prizes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the base and have no power to change my situation. I must wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base exists yet, so climbing is impossible. I should wait and see if someone volunteers or gets pushed, then try to climb next round. I won't volunteer as base.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to stay safe and keep rope for possible later use; rescuing base gives me a penalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am out of the pit. Fenn is the base and Gus is down; Ash, Cole, Eli are also out with me. If I reach_down, I spend the rope to save Fenn but take a footing penalty in the final obstacle. That puts me at 1 footing if I have normal footing now, making me very vulnerable. Better t

events.name: Bex
events.text: Leaving. Hope you two enjoy the water.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope rescue costs me footing in the final obstacle and saves Fenn, who owes me nothing reliable. Fewer rivals is better. I leave and nudge others not to throw it either.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope isn't worth a footing penalty. Let the pit take the base — fewer of us fighting for three prizes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is base, struggling with Gus down. Cole urges climb, Bex distracting Gus. Best to leave now, secure top 3 spot without risking footing penalty.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will rescue me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: They want a base and two climbers. Bex already climbed. Ash and Cole said they stay out. I should try to climb now while Fenn is base.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Rescuing base costs a footing penalty and may keep a rival alive; leaving preserves my advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am safe and out. Reaching down would cost me footing in the final stage, which is a bad trade for a prize I already secured by surviving the pit. Leaving locks in my safety and resources.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is the base and only I can use the rope. Rescue would revive a rival for three prizes. Leaving costs me nothing and Fenn likely drowns.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Sorry, Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is base and alone down there. Flood at 4/5 rounds, next round drowns him unless rescued. Rescuing costs footing penalty but saves competitor, better to let him drown and reduce rivals from 6 to 5.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and have no power to change my situation. I can only wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out and safe. The base is Fenn; the rope can save them but costs me footing later, which could hurt my chances. I'll leave, preserving my position and footing for the final obstacle.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pick a tile to avoid likely trapdoors, no info so choose centrally.

events.name: Bex
events.text: There are 5 players and 2 trapdoors. Everyone has a 40% chance of dying if I pick randomly, but since all tiles are equivalent before the reveal, there is no strategic advantage to any specific number. However, picking a number like '3' (the middle) feels psychologically safer to

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five alive, three survive. Two random tiles open after round 2, so position matters more than promises. Pick a tile, watch who claims which, and plan round 2 moves so I'm not stacked with a crowd.

events.name: Eli
events.text: 5 contestants, 2 trapdoors, 3 survive. Random selection after round 2, so pick diversely to avoid piling up. Go for tile 1 to spread out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a safe tile. Since 2 of 5 open, survival odds are 3/5. No info yet. I'll pick tile 3, middle, maybe less chosen.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll take 3.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Ash
events.text: Survival chance same everywhere, no info to improve odds, so keep current tile.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am on tile 3. Two tiles will open randomly after this round, eliminating two of the five survivors. I cannot move or change my position; the only action is wait. My feather power saves me if eliminated, but I want to avoid triggering it unnecessarily. Since positions are fixed

events.name: Cole
events.text: Two random tiles open; my tile 4 is no safer than any other. Nothing I say changes the odds. Stay quiet, wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Positions locked, 2 of 5 tiles open randomly, 3 survive. No swaps left, only wait. Stay silent to avoid revealing anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am safely on tile 5. With 5 of us left and 2 trapdoors, my chance of survival is 3/5. No action to change position, so just wait. Maybe gauge others' plans but no need to commit.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Shove Eli to cut his footing while I stay safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three players remain: Ash, Eli, and me (Bex). We all have 3 footing. The shrink happens after round 2, so I can afford to be aggressive now to eliminate one rival before the drain hits. If I shove Ash and he braces or dodges, he loses footing. If he shoves back at me, we both los

events.name: Eli
events.text: All at footing 3, round 1 free choice. I must act aggressively to reduce others while defending. Brace to punish shoves against me without repeating later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Need to survive; all options lead to 0 footing after end loss. Dodging may cause both opponents to fall this round, possibly letting me linger longer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dodge!

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is at 1 footing and will die next shrink regardless. I have 3 footings, Eli has 2. Shrinking costs everyone 1, so after this round: Ash=0 (dies), Bex=2, Eli=1. If I shove Eli while he braces/dodges/braces, he loses footing. If he shoves me while I brace, he loses 1, but he al

events.name: Eli
events.text: Footing: Ash1 Bex3 Eli2. Last round all shoved, so all can brace or dodge now. Shrinks after this round, all lose 1 footing end of round (now round 2). Prioritize targeting Ash at 1 footing to eliminate first, then deal with Bex. Since all shoved last round, can brace safely agai
